evidence: Only 2 top-level packages (coursera, coursera.test), indicating a single deployable unit
Clear module separation by concern (api, cookies, credentials, downloaders, workflow, etc.) with well-defined responsibilities
High average fan-out (5.93) suggests tight internal coupling within the monolith but low external coupling
Test directory nested under main package, typical of modular monoliths with integrated testing
No evidence of inter-service communication patterns (no REST clients to external services beyond Coursera API, no message queues, no service discovery)
Single entry point (coursera_dl.py) orchestrating components, consistent with monolithic architecture
Shared domain models (e.g., Asset namedtuple, various V1/V2 classes) used across modules
Directory depth of 3 indicates reasonable modularity without excessive nesting
risks: High fan-out may indicate modules with too many dependencies, potentially violating separation of concerns
Lack of clear architectural boundaries could lead to technical debt if modules become too entangled over time
Testing is integrated but not isolated, making it harder to verify module boundaries
